with open("input.bin", "wb") as f:
    f.write(poc_data)

analyzed_vuln.description: Double-free of alias flag arrays caused by storing an allocated flags pointer in aliasf even when decode_flags() reports an invalid numeric flag list (e.g., negative value). In FLAG_NUM mode, decode_flags() allocates `new unsigned short[len]` and can set parsed entries to 0 for invalid inputs like `-25`, but still returns a nonzero length and non-null pointer. parse_aliasf() accepts this as success and pushes the pointer into `aliasf`. Later, dictionary entries using `/1` retrieve that same pointer via get_aliasf(); during HashMgr::free_table(), free_flag() deletes it as if it were per-entry-owned flags (because TESTAFF(...ONLYUPCASEFLAG...) can evaluate true on crafted data). Finally HashMgr::~HashMgr() iterates aliasf and deletes the same pointer again, triggering double-free at destructor line ~133.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: PoV must enable numeric flags (`FLAG num`), define an AF alias table (`AF 1`) with a malformed/negative numeric alias payload (`AF -25,5`), and then reference alias index 1 from a dictionary entry (`/1`). Data flow: affdicfuzzer input -> HashMgr::load_config -> parse_aliasf/decode_flags allocates alias buffer -> alias pointer saved in aliasf -> load_tables/add_word stores same pointer in hash entries -> destruction path calls free_table/free_flag then destructor frees aliasf again.
